question: India ranks ________ in the Energy Transition Index 2025.
solution:
The correct answer is __**71st**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's rank in the Energy Transition Index (ETI) 2025** is **71st**, reflecting its progress and challenges in transitioning to a sustainable energy system.
 
• The **Energy Transition Index (ETI)** is published annually by the **World Economic Forum (WEF)** in collaboration with Accenture.
 
• The index evaluates countries based on their **energy system performance** and their readiness for transition to clean and sustainable energy sources.
 
• The ETI ranking is determined by analyzing factors such as **energy security, affordability, environmental sustainability, and economic development**.
 
• India's rank of **71st** highlights its significant efforts in renewable energy deployment but also points to areas requiring improvement, such as reducing dependence on coal and enhancing energy efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Energy Transition Index (ETI):**

 
 
• The ETI ranks countries on the basis of their energy transition readiness and system performance.
 
• It focuses on a country's ability to build a sustainable, secure, and inclusive energy system.
 
• The index takes into account factors such as **policy frameworks, investment in renewables, technological innovation**, and public-private collaboration.
 
 
 
• **India's Renewable Energy Initiatives:**
 
 
• India has set a target of achieving **500 GW of renewable energy capacity** by 2030, which includes solar, wind, biomass, and hydroelectric power.
 
• It is among the top 5 countries in terms of renewable energy capacity installation globally.
 
• Initiatives like the **National Solar Mission** and the **International Solar Alliance (ISA)** underscore India's commitment to clean energy.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Energy Transition:**
 
 
• High dependency on coal for power generation, which accounts for over **50%** of India's energy mix.
 
• Limited grid infrastructure and storage capacity for renewable energy.
 
• Balancing economic growth with environmental sustainability remains a complex challenge.
 
 
 
• **Global Leaders in ETI:**
 
 
• Countries like **Sweden, Norway, and Denmark** consistently rank at the top of the ETI due to their advanced clean energy systems, policy frameworks, and high levels of investment in sustainable technologies.
 
• These nations have successfully reduced their reliance on fossil fuels and prioritized environmental sustainability.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **World Economic Forum (WEF):**

 
 
• The WEF is a global organization that engages business, political, academic, and other leaders to shape global, regional, and industry agendas.
 
• It is headquartered in **Geneva, Switzerland**, and is well-known for hosting the annual **Davos Summit**.
 
 
 
• **India's Energy Mix:**
 
 
• Coal is the dominant source of energy, contributing to around **55%** of the power generation.
 
• Renewables, including solar and wind, contribute approximately **25%** to the energy mix.
 
• The government aims to achieve **net zero carbon emissions** by 2070.
 
 
 
• **Energy Transition Goals:**
 
 
• Developing countries like India face unique challenges in transitioning to cleaner energy systems while ensuring equitable access and economic growth.
 
• Strengthening public-private partnerships and fostering innovation are key to achieving sustainable energy targets.
